title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: open — reply to OT arguments for imputing Adam's actual sin
pass_a_gloss: Cap. VIII opens Placeus's reply to arguments drawn from the Old Testament (his opponent's Cap. V) for imputing Adam's actual sin. With the status of the question set out as the learned man pleased, Placeus says that in his fifth chapter he now draws his argument-forces into the field and unfolds them. First in line come a few drawn from the Old Testament.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER VIII. Reply to the arguments which for the Imputation of Adam's Actual sin are drawn from the Old Testament, Cap. V. The status of the question having been constituted and illustrated as it seemed good to you, at length, most distinguished Sir, in the fifth chapter of your treatise you draw the forces of your arguments into the field and unfold them. And first of all there come forth a few drawn from the Old Testament.
source_text: CAPUT VIII. Responsio ad argumenta quae pro Imputatione peccati Actualis Adami ducuntur ex Vetere Testamento Cap. V. Constituto & illustrato, prout tibi visum est, quaestionis statu, tandem, Vir Clarissime, Capite tui tractatus quinto copias argumentorum tuorum educis in aciem, & explicas. Prodeunt autem omnium prima pauca quaedam e Vetere Testamento deprompta.
